title: Listening Comprehension
intro: Listen to a dialogue, then answer multiple choice questions. Listen for details (numbers, times, names), but also for reasons, feelings, and what the speakers will do next. These are generated review dialogues on Module 1 topics, because the quiz dialogue is only played in class.

lines.speaker: Ava
lines.text: Leo, why does your robot keep making that popping noise? It sounds like an old car.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: The motor sputters every time I turn it on. I have tried three batteries, and it still stops after ten seconds.

lines.speaker: Ava
lines.text: So the battery is not the problem. Did you check the wires?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Not yet. Honestly, I was ready to give up. My first design was a complete flop, and this one is not much better.

lines.speaker: Ava
lines.text: Don't say that. Thomas Edison tested thousands of materials before his incandescent bulb worked. He called every failure a lesson.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: That is easy to say when you are Edison.

lines.speaker: Ava
lines.text: He was not Edison when he started, either. Look, the science fair is on the twentieth. That gives you eleven days.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Okay. This weekend I will take the whole thing apart, check every wire, and build a new prototype with a bigger battery.

lines.speaker: Ava
lines.text: And if it works, you should apply for a patent so nobody can copy your gadget.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: A patent? Ava, first I need it to run for more than ten seconds!

lines.speaker: Ava
lines.text: Fine. Ten seconds first, patent later. I will bring my dad's toolbox on Saturday.

questions.q: What problem does Leo's robot have?
choices: It is too heavy to carry.
It cannot be turned on at all.
The motor sputters and stops after ten seconds.

questions.q: Why does Ava say the battery is probably NOT the problem?
choices: Because the robot has no battery
Because Leo already tried three batteries

questions.q: How does Leo feel at the beginning of the conversation?
choices: Discouraged and ready to give up

questions.q: Why does Ava talk about Thomas Edison?
choices: To show that failures are part of inventing and Leo should keep going
To explain how a light bulb works
To tell Leo to build a light bulb instead
To prove that Leo's robot is a flop

questions.q: When is the science fair?
choices: On the twentieth, eleven days away

questions.q: What does Leo mean when he says, "That is easy to say when you are Edison"?
choices: He wants to be called Edison.
He thinks Edison was a bad inventor.
He thinks it was easier for a famous inventor than for him.
He does not know who Edison was.

questions.q: What will happen on Saturday?
choices: Leo will apply for a patent.
Ava will buy a new robot.
Ava will bring her dad's toolbox and they will rebuild the robot.

lines.speaker: Mr. Chen
lines.text: Molly, I heard you want to start a recycling club. Tell me about it.

lines.speaker: Molly
lines.text: Yes! Last week I counted the trash in the cafeteria. We fill six big bags every lunch, and about half of it is paper and plastic bottles.

lines.speaker: Mr. Chen
lines.text: Six bags a day? That is a lot more than I expected.

lines.speaker: Molly
lines.text: That is why my objective is to cut the cafeteria trash in half by December.

lines.speaker: Mr. Chen
lines.text: That is a big goal for one semester. How will you begin?

lines.speaker: Molly
lines.text: First, I will put a labeled bin next to every trash can, one for paper and one for bottles. Then I will give a short talk in the auditorium so everyone knows what goes where.

lines.speaker: Mr. Chen
lines.text: Some students will not listen to a talk. What about them?

lines.speaker: Molly
lines.text: I thought about that. The class that recycles the most each month wins ten extra minutes of recess.

lines.speaker: Mr. Chen
lines.text: Now that will get their attention. You are evidently very passionate about this.

lines.speaker: Molly
lines.text: My cousin's town started recycling forty percent more after one girl began a club. If she can do it, so can we.

lines.speaker: Mr. Chen
lines.text: All right. I can order the bins, but you need to write the talk yourself. Bring me a draft by Friday.

lines.speaker: Molly
lines.text: Deal. Every small contribution makes a difference.

questions.q: How much trash does the cafeteria make every lunch?
What is Molly's objective?
choices: To cut the cafeteria trash in half by December
To give a speech every day

questions.q: Why is Mr. Chen surprised?
choices: Molly is too young to start a club.
The cafeteria makes more trash than he expected.

questions.q: What is Molly's plan for students who will not listen to her talk?
choices: She will take away their lunch.
She will give the talk twice.
The class that recycles the most wins extra recess.

questions.q: Why does Molly mention her cousin's town?
choices: To explain where she was born
To show that one person's club really can make a big difference
To ask Mr. Chen for a trip

questions.q: What does Mr. Chen agree to do?
What must Molly do by Friday?
choices: Bring Mr. Chen a draft of her talk

lines.speaker: Coach Rivera
lines.text: Welcome to tryouts, Sam. Have you played wheelchair basketball before?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Only in my cousin's driveway. He plays for a club team, and he can maneuver his chair around anyone.

lines.speaker: Coach Rivera
lines.text: Good. Then you know the two-push rule. Push twice, then you must dribble, pass, or shoot.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: I know it, but I forget it when I get excited. My cousin says I travel more than a school bus.

lines.speaker: Coach Rivera
lines.text: We will fix that. A lot of new players think speed and acceleration matter most. They do not. Passing matters more.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Really? I thought you would want the fastest players.

lines.speaker: Coach Rivera
lines.text: A fast player who loses the ball helps the other team. Let's see you pass to Jordan while you are moving.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Okay. Should I push forward while I pass, or stop first?

lines.speaker: Coach Rivera
lines.text: Keep moving. And keep your eyes up, not on your wheels. Nice! That was a clean pass.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Thanks. My impulse was to look down, but I remembered what you said.

lines.speaker: Coach Rivera
lines.text: That is exactly the habit I am looking for. Practice is Tuesdays and Thursdays at four. Can you make both?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Tuesdays are fine. On Thursdays I have piano until four thirty, but I can come right after.

lines.speaker: Coach Rivera
lines.text: Thirty minutes late is better than not at all. See you Tuesday.

questions.q: Where has Sam played wheelchair basketball before?
What is the two-push rule?
choices: A player may only push twice in a game.
After two pushes, a player must dribble, pass, or shoot.
Two players must push the ball together.
A player must pass after every push.

questions.q: What does Sam mean when he says he "travels more than a school bus"?
choices: He rides the bus to practice.
He often breaks the two-push rule.
He is faster than a bus.

questions.q: According to the coach, what matters most?
Why does the coach say a fast player who loses the ball helps the other team?
choices: Because the coach does not like speed
Because the other team likes fast players
Because losing the ball gives the other team a chance to score

questions.q: Why is the coach pleased with Sam at the end?
choices: Sam remembered to keep his eyes up instead of following his impulse.

questions.q: What will Sam do on Thursdays?
choices: Come to practice about thirty minutes late, after piano

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Did you finish the chapter about William and the windmill?

lines.speaker: Noah
lines.text: I did. I could not stop reading. His village was impoverished, and then the rain stopped, so the crops died.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: And his family could not pay for school anymore. That was the part that got me. He was only fourteen.

lines.speaker: Noah
lines.text: Right, so he went to the library instead. He found a picture of a windmill in a science book, and he could barely read the English.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: But he understood the picture. That is what I think the author wants us to notice. He learned from the diagram, not the words.

lines.speaker: Noah
lines.text: He built the first one out of junk: an old bicycle, a fan blade, and pipes from the scrap yard. People in the village said he was crazy. Even his mother was worried.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: They called him eccentric, but the windmill made enough electricity to light his house. Then what happened?

lines.speaker: Noah
lines.text: Later he built a bigger one that pumped water to irrigate the fields, so the village could grow food even without rain.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: So the same people who laughed at him ended up drinking his water.

lines.speaker: Noah
lines.text: Exactly. That is why I think the story is called Winds of Hope. The wind did not change. What changed was that one boy refused to give up.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Let's use that as our central idea for the poster. Can you draw the windmill?

lines.speaker: Noah
lines.text: If you write the sentences. Meet in the library at lunch?

questions.q: What two problems did William's village have?
choices: It had too much rain and too many schools.
The trains stopped and the school burned down.
The library closed and the roads flooded.
It was impoverished, and the rain stopped so the crops died.

questions.q: Why did William go to the library instead of school?
choices: His family could no longer pay for school.
He was too old for school.
The school was too far away.

questions.q: According to Grace, what does the author want readers to notice?
choices: The library had many science books.
William learned from the diagram even though he could barely read the words.
William liked pictures more than words.

questions.q: How did the villagers feel about William at first?
choices: They gave him money for parts.
They thought he was crazy and called him eccentric.
They asked him to build them windmills.

questions.q: What did the bigger windmill do?
choices: Pumped water to irrigate the fields

questions.q: What does Grace mean when she says the people "ended up drinking his water"?
choices: The same people who laughed at him later benefited from his invention.
The windmill made the water taste better.

questions.q: According to Noah, why is the story called Winds of Hope?
choices: The book is about the weather.
The wind was the same, but one boy who refused to give up changed everything.

questions.q: What will Grace and Noah do next?
choices: Meet in the library at lunch to make a poster

lines.speaker: Ms. Park
lines.text: Class, a safety inspector is coming on Thursday morning. She will check the science lab and the auditorium.

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.text: Are we in trouble? Is that why she is coming?

lines.speaker: Ms. Park
lines.text: Not at all. Inspectors visit every school in the district once a year. Their job is to find problems before anyone gets hurt.

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.text: So what does she look for?

lines.speaker: Ms. Park
lines.text: Things like blocked exits, broken plugs, chemicals stored in the wrong cabinet. Last year she found a fire extinguisher that was ten years old.

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.text: Ten years! Did it still work?

lines.speaker: Ms. Park
lines.text: Nobody wanted to find out. The school replaced it the same week. That is exactly why her visit is useful.

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.text: Can we help get ready?

lines.speaker: Ms. Park
lines.text: Yes. Today I need two volunteers to take the boxes away from the back door of the lab. Tomorrow I need someone to check that every plug cover in the room is on.

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.text: I can do the boxes today, but tomorrow I have a dentist appointment in the afternoon.

lines.speaker: Ms. Park
lines.text: Then do the plugs in the morning before class starts. And Diego, please do not move the chemicals. That part is for adults only.

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.text: Got it. Boxes today, plugs tomorrow morning, no chemicals.

questions.q: When is the inspector coming?
Why does Diego ask, "Are we in trouble?"
choices: He does not like Ms. Park.
He thinks the inspector is coming because the class did something wrong.

questions.q: According to Ms. Park, what is an inspector's job?
choices: To find problems before anyone gets hurt

questions.q: What did the inspector find last year?
choices: A fire extinguisher that was ten years old

questions.q: What does Ms. Park mean when she says, "Nobody wanted to find out"?
choices: The inspector did not tell anyone.
It was safer to replace the extinguisher than to test whether it still worked.

questions.q: What will Diego do today?
choices: Move the boxes away from the lab's back door

questions.q: Why will Diego check the plugs in the morning instead of the afternoon?
choices: The lab is closed in the afternoon.
The inspector comes in the afternoon.
He has a dentist appointment in the afternoon.

questions.q: Which job is for adults only?
